## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

SuttaCentral records several resembling parallels to verses within the text in other early Buddhist verse collections. These include the Pali *Dhammapada* (Dhp 339 and Dhp 340), the Patna Dharmapada (*Śaraṇavagga*, verses 216–238), verses 61–70 of the Gāndhārī Dharmapada, the Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the *Udānavarga* (specifically the *Cittavarga* and *Tṛṣṇavarga*), and corresponding Chinese translations of the *Dharmapada* and *Udānavarga* traditions (T 210.32, T 212.3, T 212.32, T 213.3, and T 213.31) [SuttaCentral].
Pali-internal text reuse calculated by DharmaNexus shows extensive shared material with the commentary in the second part of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0508a2), amounting to 19 matching passages and 4,802 shared characters covering segments 0.4–22.5 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects machine alignments with the Tibetan *Ārya-saddharmānusmṛtyupasthāna* (D0287-2) and the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26), though these represent lower-scoring automated alignments rather than established direct parallels [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
